strategicFrame.employerBrand: Continuity-focused AGPAL-accredited community general practice in Brisbane’s inner south
hardGuards: Do not publish percentage/earnings claims on public pages
Do not imply the practice issues Medicare provider numbers
Do not promise registrar places without capacity confirmation
Prefer operational proof (nursing, reception, AGPAL, sessions) over perk language

personas.name: Early Career GP
personas.archetype: Recently fellowed or early post-fellowship GP building a sustainable list
motivations: Build a patient list with continuity rather than high-volume churn
Learn sustainable consulting habits with nursing and reception support
Find a practice with clear onboarding and AGPAL-aligned systems
Develop clinical confidence across general practice presentations
concerns: Will I get enough support without losing clinical autonomy?
How long will it take to build a viable list?
Are commercial terms fair for someone still establishing?
Provider number / location paperwork feel opaque
informationNeeded: Onboarding pathway and first-90-day expectations
Nursing and reception support model
How patient allocation / continuity works for new GPs
Session options and growth over time
What the practice can/cannot do on provider numbers (Services Australia)
preferredContent: GP FAQ (billing discussed privately; provider number honesty)
Meet the team / team-based care pages
objections: I need more structure than a busy private-billing mill offers
I’m worried I’ll be left alone without mentorship culture
I don’t want a practice that only chases throughput
I’m unsure about paperwork and start timing

recommendedWebsiteMessaging.headline: Build your practice where continuity still matters.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.supportingLine: Supported consulting, AGPAL-aligned systems, and a team that helps patients return to you — not a high-volume clinic.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.cta: Express interest as an early-career GP
proofPoints: Nursing and reception support around the consult
Session growth as your list develops
Clear onboarding conversation — no agency marketplace
avoid: Over-promising mentorship programs not actually run

personas.name: Established GP Seeking Change
personas.archetype: Experienced VR GP leaving a practice culture, workload, or values mismatch
motivations: Restore clinical meaning and continuity after burnout or throughput pressure
Join a stable team with professional respect and operational reliability
Protect consulting quality without giving up income sustainability
Relocate or reset within Brisbane’s inner south
concerns: Will commercial terms match my experience?
Can I transfer or rebuild a list without starting from zero forever?
Is the culture genuinely collaborative or just marketed that way?
Will governance feel bureaucratic rather than enabling?
informationNeeded: Honest description of patient community and continuity model
How private commercial conversations work (no public % claims)
Room, nursing, and reception capacity for experienced GPs
AGPAL / quality posture as signal of operational maturity
Session footprint options for a full or near-full week
objections: I’ve heard continuity language before — show me the operating model
I won’t move for vague culture claims
I need a serious commercial discussion, not a careers brochure
I’m cautious about network practices diluting local identity

recommendedWebsiteMessaging.headline: A professional home for experienced general practice.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.supportingLine: If you are seeking a change toward continuity, clinical respect and dependable team support, talk with us directly.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.cta: Start a confidential conversation with the practice
proofPoints: Nursing and reception that protect consulting time
Local Woolloongabba identity within a wider healthcare network

personas.name: Returning GP
personas.archetype: GP returning from leave, travel, parental pause, illness, or non-clinical period
personas.likelyStage: Variable; often VR with a gap in recent consulting
motivations: Re-enter practice at a sustainable pace
Rebuild confidence with supportive nursing/reception systems
Find a practice that respects a staged return
Reconnect with continuity-based community care
concerns: Will my gap be judged harshly?
Can I start with fewer sessions and grow?
Are clinical systems and MBS workflows easy to relearn here?
What documentation and provider-number steps do I need?
informationNeeded: Staged session options and start-window flexibility
Orientation / billing familiarisation support (practice-led, not PN issuance)
Document checklist for onboarding readiness
Nursing support for procedures and preventive pathways
Honest capacity: when rooms and cover allow a return
preferredContent: Expression of interest with space for return context
objections: I need a soft landing, not a full book on week one
I’m anxious about systems after time away
I don’t want to be treated as a locum temporary fill

recommendedWebsiteMessaging.headline: Return to practice with a staged, supported start.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.supportingLine: Tell us where you are in your return. We discuss sessions, orientation and timing openly — without treating you as a short-term stopgap.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.cta: Share your return timeline in an expression of interest
proofPoints: Flexible sessions that can grow over time
Clear separation: practice onboarding vs Services Australia provider numbers
avoid: Assuming every returner wants full-time immediately
Implying the practice can fast-track provider numbers

personas.name: Part-Time Parent GP
personas.archetype: VR GP balancing parenting (or caring) with sustainable consulting sessions
personas.likelyStage: Often mid-career; strong preference for predictable part-time footprint
motivations: Predictable sessions that fit school / care routines
Meaningful continuity without full-time burnout
A practice that treats part-time as real membership, not leftover slots
Reliable nursing/reception so shorter days still feel clinically complete
concerns: Will part-time GPs get poor rooms or leftover patients only?
Can sessions stay stable term-to-term?
Will I be pressured to expand hours before I’m ready?
Is parking / commute workable for school-run timing?
informationNeeded: Examples of sustainable part-time session patterns
How continuity works when consulting fewer days
Parking and location practicalities (468 Vulture Street)
Team cover when you are not on site
Commercial discussion process for part-time arrangements
preferredContent: EOI form prompting preferred sessions / days
objections: Part-time often means second-class in other clinics
I can’t do unpredictable weekend/evening expansion
I need reliability more than maximum billings language

recommendedWebsiteMessaging.headline: Part-time general practice that still feels like belonging.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.supportingLine: Stable sessions, team support and continuity for patients — without treating part-time GPs as temporary cover.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.cta: Tell us your preferred days and session pattern
proofPoints: Part-time arrangements discussed as lasting practice membership
Inner-south location with parking and transport options
Nursing and reception that make shorter consulting days workable
avoid: Pressure language about ramping to full-time

personas.name: Special Interest GP
personas.archetype: GP wanting to deepen a clinical interest inside community general practice
personas.likelyStage: Any career stage with a defined interest area
motivations: Practise broader GP care while developing an interest (e.g. women’s health, skin, mental health, procedural, children’s health)
Serve local patient need rather than run a boutique specialty shop
Access nursing/procedure support where relevant
Join a practice that welcomes interest without forcing a marketplace brand
concerns: Will my interest be supported with rooms, nursing and equipment?
Will I be siloed away from general practice continuity?
Are credentialing and scope expectations clear?
Is there genuine community demand here?
informationNeeded: How clinical interests are welcomed within scope and credentialing
Nursing/procedure support for relevant interests
Balance between interest work and general consulting
Examples of interests that fit local community care
EOI pathway to describe interests without a specialty job board feel
preferredContent: Services / knowledge pages that show community need
GP FAQ + EOI with interests field
objections: I don’t want a recruitment marketplace for niche roles
Interest work without nursing support isn’t viable
I still want to be a GP first, not a single-issue clinician

recommendedWebsiteMessaging.headline: Bring clinical depth that strengthens community care.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.supportingLine: Special interests are welcome when they serve local patients and sit within safe scope — inside general practice, not instead of it.
recommendedWebsiteMessaging.cta: Share your clinical interests in an expression of interest
proofPoints: Interest areas discussed against patient need and team capacity
Nursing support for procedures and preventive pathways where appropriate
Continuity remains the practice centre of gravity
avoid: Listing interests as productised service SKUs for recruitment
Implying every interest is automatically resourced
